positions.name: KnowledgeErasureDirective
positions.frame: Is the speaker enacting authority by commanding erasure of what is known and declaring the official history closed?
positions.why: All three expressions cohere under one relational read: the speaker positions themselves as able to order erasure of records (src-1, src-2) and then ratify that order by declaring the institutional history settled (src-3). The set holds a conviction gradient — src-1 and src-2 are decision-grade imperatives commanding a future state of removal, while src-3 is a claim-grade assertion about a settled past — but the authority-ranking frame holds both sides: the command to forget and the declaration that nothing happened are the same act of controlling the record. The tension between irrealis directive and realis assertion is the shape of the position, not a defect.
